title: UK's GDP grows 0.4% in July, retail trade falls 0.5%
summary:
UK real GDP grew 0.4 per cent in July 2026, extending expansion for an eighth consecutive three-month period. 
However, retail trade excluding motor vehicles fell 0.5 per cent, signalling softer consumer activity. 
Services grew 0.6 per cent over three months, while production and construction each contracted 0.5 per cent, highlighting a mixed economic backdrop for apparel and retail demand.

title: How Bangladesh’s yarn curbs exposed sharp industry fault lines
summary:
Bangladesh’s NBR has tightened duty-free 10–30 count cotton yarn imports under the bond facility for export-oriented readymade garment factories.
Spinners say the move will lift demand for local yarn, revive mills, boost value addition, conserve foreign currency and support jobs.
BGMEA and BKMEA warn bank guarantees may raise costs, disrupt shipments and weaken garment export competitiveness.

title: US inflation, interest-rate uncertainty cloud cotton market outlook
summary:
US inflation and interest-rate uncertainty are clouding the cotton market outlook despite resilient garment spending. 
Cotton-dominant apparel imports fell 11.4 per cent YoY in July, while import costs remained 12 per cent above pre-pandemic levels. 
Elevated inflation, tariffs and slower wage growth are prompting more cautious sourcing decisions across the cotton and apparel supply chain.

title: US T&A import volume falls 8.5% in January-July 2026
summary:
US textile and apparel import volumes across all fibre types fell 8.51 per cent YoY to 54,263.259 million SME in January–July 2026, OTEXA data showed.
Apparel imports declined 9.12 per cent, while non-apparel textiles dropped 8.31 per cent; cotton and MMF product imports also fell.
Exports declined 6.47 per cent, with apparel shipments up but fabric and yarn exports lower.

title: US retail import season extends as cargo rises 9.6% in September 2026
summary:
US retail import peak season is extending, with September forecast at 2.31 million TEU, up 9.6 per cent year on year and potentially 2026’s busiest month.
Delays linked to China weather and Panama Canal rerouting are shifting cargo timing.
Retailers face elevated port volumes despite tariffs, inflation and high fuel prices before an expected October easing.

title: Netherlands inland waterway freight falls 18.8% in Aug amid drought
summary:
Netherlands inland waterway freight fell nearly 19 per cent in summer 2026 as drought cut river levels and vessel loads despite more journeys.
Cross-border flows were hit most: August imports fell 20.2 per cent, exports 22.2 per cent and transit trade 50.1 per cent.
Germany-linked Rhine traffic saw steepest losses; Belgium flows rose, signalling route risk for textile and apparel supply chains.

title: Netherlands' GHG emissions rise 0.6% in Q2 2026
summary:
Netherlands GHG emissions rose 0.6 per cent year on year in Q2 2026, as power-sector increases outweighed mobility cuts.
Electricity emissions climbed nearly 22 per cent on higher coal and gas use, while manufacturing emissions slipped 1 per cent.
Freight, manufacturing and sourcing teams face shifting emissions exposure across transport, power and industrial activity.

title: Fashion must count 80% of fibre; but can it prove where it comes from?
summary:
From 2027, Action Cohort brands and retailers must set targets across priority materials covering at least 80 per cent of their portfolio.
TexPro shows import exposure in raw cotton, raw wool, viscose and polyester staple is concentrated in a few origins.
Raw-material origin was unknown for 76 per cent of cotton, 82 per cent of polyester, 87 per cent of nylon and 82 per cent of viscose.

title: Bangladesh made $6.8 bn from jute in 10 yrs; why curb raw exports now?
summary:

TexPro shows HS 5303 exports fell 40.5 per cent to about $79.0 million in FY2025-26, while the four selected jute categories declined roughly 10 per cent.
The $5-7 billion processing goal needs 5.7-fold to nearly eightfold growth from $883.69 million in FY2025-26 exports.

title: Australian wool market ends lower as buyers turn selective
summary:
Australia’s wool market ended Week 11 lower as the EMI fell 12 cents to 1,878 A¢/kg after Wednesday losses erased early gains.
National offerings dropped to 23,486 bales, with 21,147 sold and the pass-in rate rising to 10.0 per cent.
Currency strength lifted the EMI in US-dollar terms, while next week’s larger offering will test demand ahead of the Nanjing conference.

title: Bangladesh apparel exports price to US drops 2.26% YoY in Jan-Jul 2026
summary:
The average price of Bangladesh’s apparel exports to the US fell by 2.26 per cent YoY in the first seven months this year. 
There was also a 6.5-per cent drop in Bangladesh's apparel export value to the US during the period, while shipment volume dropped by 4.34 per cent YoY. 
Not all exporters bore the additional tariff burden equally; in some cases, buyers and exporters shared the cost.

summary:
Middle East disruptions lifted Inditex’s transport and input costs in the first half, affecting gross margin and operating expenditure in the second quarter.
The Zara owner has 480 franchise stores in the Middle East, all open, but geopolitical conditions are impacting regional sales.
First-half gross margin rose 40 basis points to 58.7 per cent, while net income increased 6.8 per cent to €3.

title: India’s US apparel exports fall 26%; Bangladesh overtakes China
summary:
In January–July 2026, US apparel imports from India fell about 26 per cent to $2.45 billion, Office of Textiles and Apparel data show.
Total US apparel imports declined roughly 9 per cent to about $41.8 billion.
Vietnam led at about $9.37 billion, while Bangladesh reached $4.66 billion and moved ahead of China.
Cambodia and Indonesia increased shipments as China fell by about one-third.

title: Argentina apparel imports rise 31.7% in Jan-Jul after liberalisation
summary:
Argentina’s apparel imports reached $468.262 million in January-July 2026, up 31.73 per cent year on year. 
China held a 52.03 per cent share, while Vietnam and Bangladesh grew 50.62 per cent and 54.52 per cent, respectively. 
Imports nearly doubled in 2025 as liberalised trade, easier payment access and price-competitive Asian hubs supported apparel sourcing.

title: US' Caleres lifts FY26 EPS outlook as Q2 sales rise 5.6%
summary:
Caleres expects low-to-mid-single-digit fiscal 2026 sales growth and lifted the lower end of adjusted EPS guidance to $1.50.
Second-quarter net sales rose 5.6 per cent to $695.5 million and GAAP net earnings reached $58.6 million, aided by tariff refunds.
Brand Portfolio sales grew 23.6 per cent, offsetting lower Famous Footwear sales amid a delayed Back-to-School season.

title: Bangladesh, US review trade & investment conditions
summary:
US envoy Brent T Christensen told Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir that US companies are keen to operate in Bangladesh.
The talks covered investment, bilateral trade, energy co-operation, import policy changes and transparency in large infrastructure projects.
For sourcing teams, the discussion points to continued focus on market access, energy supply and business-process reform.

title: US' Lands' End returns to profit as Q2 revenue rises to $302 mn
summary:

US e-commerce led growth, rising 9.0 per cent to $182.4 million; Outfitters gained, while third-party sales dropped 20.4 per cent.
Lands' End reaffirmed FY26 guidance, with inventory up 13 per cent for seasonal build as operations normalised before the holiday season.

title: US apparel imports are weak; so why did bookings jump 79%?
summary:
US HS61–62 apparel imports fell 7.77 per cent to $36.90 billion in H1 2026, but the contraction narrowed from 11.82 per cent in Q1 to 3.28 per cent in Q2.
Clothing and accessories-store sales rose 5.9 per cent to $151.09 billion; June's inventory-to-sales ratio fell to 2.14.
US-bound HS61–62 ocean bookings reached 21,434 TEU in June, up 79 per cent, led by Vietnam and Cambodia.

title: Australia’s apparel imports dip 7.5% in July 2026
summary:
Australia’s apparel imports fell 7.57 per cent to Au$1.025 billion in July 2026; textile yarn, fabrics and made-up imports eased 2.58 per cent.
Fibre imports edged up to Au$12 million, while textile fibre exports declined 9.92 per cent to Au$629 million, Australian Bureau of Statistics data showed.
Fiscal 2025–26 saw apparel imports down 4.60 per cent and fibre exports up 7.72 per cent.

title: Bangladesh’s RMG sector bets on technology for a productivity edge
summary:

Some factories report gains of up to 25 per cent versus manual monitoring, though results vary by technology, conditions and measurement.
The shift also raises concerns over worker pressure, privacy and fair sharing of productivity gains.
